text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's on Monday affirmed state-controlled Swedish bank Nordbanken's senior unsecured debt rating at A with outlook stable.

"Standard & Poor's today has affirmed its single 'A' senior unsecured debt, long-term counterparty, and its A-1 short-term debt and counterparty ratings for Nordbanken and its related entities," S&P said in a statement.
"The short-term commercial paper rating for Industrikredit is affirmed at 'K-1'," it said.
The rating comes in the wake of the bank's announcement last week that it planned a five-billion crown buy back of its own shares which prompted a rally in its stock on the Swedish sharemarket.
S&P said the buy back would keep the bank's capitalisation at a good level.

"While this redemption of shares reduces the bank's Tier 1 capital ratio to just over seven percent from 9.7 percent, S&P considers that the bank's capitalisation remains at a good level and will strengthen rapidly from future profit retentions," the credit rating agency said.
S&P said the ratings reflected the bank's stand-alone position as government ownership was removed as a rating factor in 1995 after the government made it clear it intended to privatise Nordbanken.
The share buy back could reduce the government's stake to 58 percent from 65.5 percent.
S&P affirmed the state's stable outlook despite competition among Swedish banks.

"S&P, however, believes that Nordbanken is well-placed to meet this challenge, having put in place a number of measures -- including tight cost control -- which will help the bank achieve a stable performance over the medium-term," it said.
Nordbanken shares were 0.5 crowns higher at 155.5 crowns at 0955 GMT.
